title_lines: 莎拉·杰西卡·帕克联手Astrea London
押注培育钻石消费市场
美国订婚戒指六成已用培育钻石

subtitles.en: We want to talk about the stuff that you guys are doing together. But I'm curious how you guys came together.
subtitles.zh: 我们想聊聊你们合作的项目。但我很好奇你们是怎么走到一起的。

subtitles.en: Because I'm sure you get pitched a lot of things. I'm sure you get pitched a lot of things.
subtitles.zh: 因为我相信你肯定收到过很多提议。肯定收到过很多提议。

subtitles.en: How is it that this kind of made sense?
subtitles.zh: 这件事是怎么变得合理的？

subtitles.en: We don't have time to tell each of our own version, but I'm fairly sure they'd be aligned anyway.
subtitles.zh: 我们没时间各讲各的版本，但我很确定它们会是一致的。

subtitles.en: I'm just curious where they said what she said that.
subtitles.zh: 我只是好奇他们是在哪里说她说那话的。
en_highlights: where they said what she said

subtitles.en: I got a call from my agent saying that this young woman had reached out and had started this business,
subtitles.zh: 我接到经纪人的电话，说这位年轻女士联系了他，并创办了这家企业，
en_highlights: got a call from my agent

subtitles.en: although it was not a brand new, newborn. And that she wanted to have a conversation about it.
subtitles.zh: 虽然它并不是全新的、刚诞生的。而且她想就此谈一谈。

subtitles.en: And it was specific around lab-grown diamonds and what she'd hoped to do with the company and how she wanted to grow it and a partnership that we might, we may or may not be able to sort out.
subtitles.zh: 具体是关于实验室培育钻石，她希望用这家公司做什么，想如何发展它，以及我们可能、也许能或不能达成的合作。

subtitles.en: And I was really intrigued and discovered how little I really knew about lab-grown diamonds.
subtitles.zh: 我真的很感兴趣，也发现我对实验室培育钻石的了解少得可怜。

subtitles.en: And most of what I knew was generally what's happening here in this country.
subtitles.zh: 而我所知道的大部分，基本上就是这个国家正在发生的情况。

subtitles.en: And the price point that it had found its success.
subtitles.zh: 以及它找到成功定位的价格点。

subtitles.en: And that was kind of how limited I was. And then I met the person who runs the masterclass.
subtitles.zh: 那差不多就是我的局限。后来我遇到了主持大师课的人。

subtitles.en: She was pretty amazing. Well, talk to us about how the acceptance of lab-grown diamonds.
subtitles.zh: 她非常出色。来谈谈实验室培育钻石的接受度吧。

subtitles.en: Because I remember doing stories a few years ago and there were either limitations, there were costs involved in terms of the creation.
subtitles.zh: 因为我记得几年前做报道时，要么有限制，要么在制造方面涉及成本。

subtitles.en: And I know there is, to some extent, too, but how it has evolved.
subtitles.zh: 我知道某种程度上现在也有，但它是如何演变的。

subtitles.en: And because when I talk to most people who get engaged today, it's a lab-grown diamond.
subtitles.zh: 因为当我与今天大多数订婚的人交谈时，都是实验室培育钻石。

subtitles.en: Well, actually, 61% of the engagement around in the US won lab-grown diamond last year.
subtitles.zh: 实际上，去年美国61%的订婚戒指是实验室培育钻石。

title_refine.style: factual clickbait for China finance audience

entities.evidence: Vogue Taiwan and jeweller.hk both render the name as 莎拉·杰西卡·帕克 in Chinese-language coverage of the Astrea London partnership.

evidence_urls: https://www.vogue.com.tw/article/sarah-jessica-parker推出鑽石珠寶-人造鑽石再次榮登話題頭條
entities.evidence: Chinese-language coverage keeps the brand in Latin script (Astrea London); jeweller.hk offers a transliteration 阿斯特雷 but it is not an established Chinese display form, so the Latin name is the safe title label.
Vogue Arabia identifies Nathalie Morrison as Astrea London's founder; no reliable Chinese display form found, so keep the English name.
Chinese media and industry reports use 培育钻石 as the standard term; 人造钻石 appears in some headlines but is a looser variant.

terms.sense: diamonds produced in a laboratory rather than mined

clip_research.source_claim: Sarah Jessica Parker says she discovered how little she really knew about lab-grown diamonds, and most of what she knew was about what's happening in the US.
clip_research.public_baseline: China is the world's largest producer of lab-grown diamonds, with India second at roughly 15% of global production; Asia Pacific held about 34.5% of the lab-grown diamond market in 2025.
clip_research.surprise_gap: A global creative director of a lab-grown diamond brand admits limited knowledge of the industry, while public data shows China dominates production — a gap between the brand's insider positioning and the actual supply-chain geography.

china_advantage.comparison: China is the largest global producer of lab-grown diamonds, ahead of India (second, ~15% of global production); Chinese HPHT rough is a key input for Indian manufacturers.

evidence.fact: Parker says she was intrigued and discovered how little she knew about lab-grown diamonds, mostly limited to what's happening in the US.

evidence.query: lab-grown diamond market share 2024 2025 global production China India
evidence.fact: India produces over three million lab-grown diamonds a year, about 15% of global production, second behind China.

evidence.query: lab-grown diamond market share 2024 2025 global production China India
evidence.fact: Indian manufacturers import rough lab-grown diamonds mainly from China (HPHT) and Dubai (CVD).

forbidden_claims: Parker is ignorant about the diamond industry
Astrea London sources diamonds from China
Parker's statement contradicts a prior public position

notes: Astrea London has no established Simplified Chinese name; keep the Latin brand name in titles.
Nathalie Morrison has no verified Chinese rendering; do not invent one.
The china_advantage angle rests on public production data, not on the transcript itself.

data_driven_lessons.source: KC桌面-视频号动态数据明细.csv, 114 rows, July 2026 local analysis
winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
